question:
Which of the following balanced equations is correct for the given reaction?

Calcium chloride + Sulphuric acid → Calcium sulphate + Hydrogen chloride
solution:
The correct answer is: CaCl₂+H₂SO₄ to CaSO₄+2HCl

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Balancing a Chemical Equation:
 
• When Calcium Chloride reacts with Sulphuric acid, It produces Calcium Sulphate and Hydrogen Chloride.
 
• CaCl₂+H₂SO₄ to CaSO₄+HCl
 
• Now, there are 2 Hydrogen atoms on the reactant's side whereas only 1 hydrogen is atom on the product's side. To balance it, Multiply HCl by 2.
 
• CaCl₂+H₂SO₄ to CaSO₄+2HCl [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] 
 
• This is a type of Double Displacement Reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
 

 Types of Chemical Reactions
 Explanation
 General Reaction
 
 
 
 

 Combination reaction
 Two or more compounds combine to form one compound.
 A + B to AB \:
 
 

 Decomposition reaction
 A complex molecule breaks down to make simpler ones.
 AB to A+B \:
 
 

 Precipitation reaction
 Two solutions of soluble salts are mixed resulting in an insoluble solid (precipitate) forming.
 A+ soluble salt B toprecipitate + soluble salt C
 
 

 Neutralization reaction
 An acid and a base react with each other. Generally, the product of this reaction is salt and water.
 Acid + Base to salt + water
 
 

 Combustion reaction
 Oxygen combines with a compound to form carbon dioxide and water. These reactions are exothermic.
 O₂ + B to CO₂+H₂O \:
 
 

 Displacement reaction
 One element takes place with another element in the compound.
 AB + C to AC + B \:
